body:
Correction: the action table declares four webmcp_* actions that the agent-browser CLI on this machine does
not have. The read-surface sweep test reports them; they are not fixed by the pipe fix in 3d6c1e6.

Observed symptom. `tests/test_agent_browser.py::test_every_read_action_is_a_command_the_real_cli_accepts`
fails, and names exactly two actions:

    webmcp_list:   webmcp list     -> Unknown command
    webmcp_result: webmcp result i1 -> Unknown command

Evidence.
- The installed CLI is agent-browser 0.35.1 (`agent-browser --version`), a native binary at
  `%APPDATA%/npm/node_modules/agent-browser/bin/agent-browser-win32-x64.exe`.
- "webmcp" appears nowhere in that CLI: not in `--help` (0 matches), and nowhere in its installed package
  tree (`grep -ril webmcp <npm>/node_modules/agent-browser/` -> no files). Every other action in the sweep --
  the whole read surface -- is accepted by it.
- So the table is not hallucinated: WebMCP is a real, documented agent-browser feature. The CLI's docs site
  (agent-browser.dev) lists a WebMCP entry under Reference. It is the installed binary that predates it.
- npm's latest is 0.38.1; this machine has 0.35.1. The four actions came in with 43ca964 ("The whole
  agent-browser surface, and how each part of it is classified", Tisone Kironget, 2026-09-22), and the table's
  own text marks them "(experimental)".

Likely root cause. Version drift, not a wrong table: the table was written against the CLI's documented
surface, and no machine here runs a CLI new enough to have WebMCP. The repo pins no agent-browser version,
so nothing catches the gap -- and a run that picks webmcp_list today spends budget on a command that cannot
work.

Candidate repairs, and why I did not pick one.
(a) Upgrade the installed CLI to a version that has WebMCP. I deliberately did not: agent-browser is also the
    browser backend for other tooling on this machine (the same CLI owns the ~/.agent-browser browser cache),
    so a global upgrade is a change with a wider blast radius than this session's scope. Not verified whether
    0.38.1 has WebMCP.
(b) Drop the four actions from the table. Wrong while a newer CLI may well have them -- it deletes capability
    the author added on purpose, from the docs.
(c) Gate them on the CLI's version, the way `available()` already asks whether the CLI is here at all. The
    adapter's own shape supports this; it is a small design change and the one I would recommend.

Suggested owner: Tisone Kironget, who wrote the table and alone can say which CLI version the project means
to target. The user's call between (a) and (c); B-2026-09-26-1 carries the queue row and the re-run command.

Not claiming this as fixed. Claiming only that the hang it was hiding is.
